blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A Social Weather Stations (SWS) survey showed fewer Filipino families being victimized by common crimes but more being victimized by cybercrimes. Ten percent of respondents reported being victimized by common crimes in June 2026, down from the 12.3 percent in March 2026, according to the SWS poll results published on Monday. It further noted that respondents reported fewer property crimes from 11.5 percent in March 2026 to 9.1 percent in June 2026; street robbery from 8.9 percent to 7.3 percent; physical violence from 1.7 percent to 1.4 percent; carnapping from 1.1 percent to 0.3 percent; and break-ins from […]...
